question: Will the summit really happen in 2027, yes or no?

lines.text: Saudi Arabia has pushed its Riyadh investment summit, the FII, back to 2027.
It comes after weeks of Houthi missile and drone strikes on the kingdom.
The so-called Davos in the Desert was due to run from 26 to 29 October.
Organisers say they want the full scale, extraordinary quality, and unforgettable impact.

scene.quote: the full scale, extraordinary quality, and unforgettable impact

lines.text: Reuters says the in-person event was scrapped.
Semafor reports big banks privately raised safety concerns with the Public Investment Fund.
Speakers were set to include Jamie Dimon, Larry Fink and Ray Dalio.
Riyadh's main airport closed on 11 October after repeated attacks.
It reopened Sunday, but Flightradar24 says 108 flights were cancelled on Monday.
In Jeddah, 50 more flights were cancelled and nearly a quarter were delayed.
In Yemen, officials say a Houthi missile strike on an army camp in Shabwa killed at least 53.
Egypt's top security body says it will help Saudi Arabia defend itself.
Will the summit really happen in 2027, yes or no?
